_note: Readable lore found in rooms (marker type 'lore'). Original text written for this fan game, following the Istvan arc's setting. Facts marked (verify) in docs/lore/owner-storyline.md apply here too. 'unlocks' sets a progression flag when read (e.g. 'crusnik' awakens the Crusnik form).

ax_orders.title: Sealed dispatch
ax_orders.text: To Father Abel Nightroad, Department of Holy Affairs. Istvan has been free of its Methuselah lord for barely a season, yet its people vanish by night into the old water tunnels. Go below. Learn who is taking them, and why. Speak of this to no one, not even our friends in the resistance, until you know whose hand moves them. — C.

hall_plaque.title: Corroded plaque
hall_plaque.text: BY DECREE OF THE COUNT: these halls carry the city's water and the city's dead. Any human found below the third bell answers to the night. The plaque has been scratched with a cross, many times, by many hands.

worshipper_note.title: Crumpled note
worshipper_note.text: They played music in the square again. Mother went to listen and did not come home. A gentle man with a violin case said the church below would keep us safe from the soldiers. He smiled so kindly. I am going down to find her.

hunter_warning.title: Scratched into the wall
hunter_warning.text: NOT MEN. Grey cloaks, red glass eyes, axes. We cut one in half and it stood up again. They are the count's old dead, wound up like clocks. Run, and do not let it see you run.

resistance_chalk.title: Resistance chalk mark
resistance_chalk.text: A rose inside a circle: the sign of Istvan's resistance. Beneath it, a list of safe houses, most of them crossed out. The last line reads: 'Sister E. — the cathedral bell tower. Trust her.'

ossuary_epitaph.title: Ossuary epitaph
ossuary_epitaph.text: Here lie those who fell when the moon's children came down upon the city. Nine hundred years since the great war, and still we bury our dead beneath the ones who killed them.

star_graffiti.title: Fresh graffiti
star_graffiti.text: WHEN THE STAR OF SORROW RISES, ISTVAN BURNS. Painted in red over an older prayer. The paint is still wet.

esther_prayer.title: A prayer, folded small
esther_prayer.text: Lord, forgive me the rifle hidden under the altar cloth. Forgive me for wanting them to suffer. Keep my brothers in the resistance alive one more night, and if You cannot, let it be me instead. — E.

music_score.title: Sheet music
music_score.text: A violin score, beautifully copied. Thin red lines have been drawn from every note to the edge of the page, like strings. In the corner, a single initial: D.

marchesa_portrait.title: Torn portrait
marchesa_portrait.text: A noblewoman in mourning silk, painted with great care. Someone has cut the canvas at her wrists, her throat and her ankles, and threaded red cord through each cut.

crusnik_legend.title: Forbidden page
crusnik_legend.text: An old page torn from a Vatican index of heresies: '...and there are said to be beings that hunger not for the blood of men, but for the blood of those who drink it. The ancients gave them a name we will not write here.' Abel reads it twice. His hand will not stop shaking. Somewhere beneath his ribs, something very old opens its eyes.

cathedral_sealed.title: Iron door
cathedral_sealed.text: The way up to the cathedral. The door is chained from the other side, and the chains are humming, as if something on the far side is pulling them tight.

well_rope.title: A frayed rope
well_rope.text: Tied to the well's iron grate from below, cut clean through. Someone wanted the way down open, and then made sure no one could climb back up.

drowned_ledger.title: Waterlogged ledger
drowned_ledger.text: Names, dates, and beside each a sum in old silver: the price paid for every citizen sent below. The last pages are in a different hand, neat and musical, signed only with a looping D.

ballroom_invitation.title: Black-edged invitation
ballroom_invitation.text: The Marchesa requests the honour of your presence at a dance beneath the city. Dress: mourning. Music will be provided. You will not be permitted to leave before the last waltz.

cellar_crest.title: The count's crest
cellar_crest.text: A wolf crowned with a crescent moon, chiselled from the cellar door and thrown in the wine. Beyond, a passage climbs toward the castle on the hill.

bone_wall.title: Wall of bones
bone_wall.text: Skulls and long bones stacked to the height of three men, packed with lime. At the top a doorway breathes cold air and, impossibly, the scent of roses. There is no ladder and no rope. Whoever goes up there does not climb like a man.

nave_requiem.title: Requiem schedule
nave_requiem.text: Nightly requiem for the souls of Istvan, by order of the cathedral chapter. Below, in a newer hand: 'The choir sings by itself now. Nobody has seen the choirmaster for a month.'

choir_score.title: A page of choral score
choir_score.text: The notes are written in red ink and the words are not Latin. Every line ends on the same chord. In the margin: 'Rehearsal. Do not wake the city yet.'

bell_ringer.title: The bell-ringer's log
bell_ringer.text: Rang vespers. Rang compline. Rang nothing at midnight, yet the bells rang. A young gentleman in green asked to see the tower; he said he admired the acoustics.

castle_gate.title: Inscription over the gate
castle_gate.text: KADAR. Carved over an older name that has been chiselled away. The stone around it is scorched, as if by a light from the sky.

castle_gate_barred.title: The barred gatehouse
castle_gate_barred.text: A portcullis of black iron. Threads finer than hair are woven through its bars; they hum when the wind blows. Whoever strung them must be cut down first.

gyula_portrait.title: A portrait in the great hall
gyula_portrait.text: A Methuselah lord and a human woman, both smiling. The canvas has been slashed across her face and carefully mended, many times.

star_of_sorrow.title: Brass plate on the machine
star_of_sorrow.text: An instrument older than the war, built to bring down the light of a star. Someone has recently cleaned every gear by hand, and written beneath the controls: 'For her. For all of them.'

spire_inscription.title: Words cut in the spire
spire_inscription.text: Two names are carved side by side in the old stone, older than the Empire. One has been scratched out and carved again, deeper, many times.

letter_docks.title: A letter to Rome (I)
letter_docks.text: Dear Esther. The Empire's air smells of iron and roses, and nobody here has offered me tea. A duchess met me at the gangplank with a sword. I think she was pleased to see me. I think. — A.

letter_market.title: A letter to Rome (II)
letter_market.text: Dear Esther. I met a young count today who bought me tea he could not afford and apologised for his grandmother. If there is going to be peace, it will look a little like him. — A.

cistern_prayers.title: Scratched on a column
cistern_prayers.text: Rows of small marks, the way prisoners count days. Under them, in a child's hand: 'The court says we are not noble enough to live in the light. The water does not mind.'

cistern_strings.title: Silver threads
cistern_strings.text: Fine wire, knotted to the columns like a spider's web, and hummed through when the water moves. The same threads Abel cut in Istvan. Whoever plays these strings has followed him across the sky.

conduit_runoff.title: Scorched stone
conduit_runoff.text: The conduit's walls are glazed black, and the water steams. Something hot is poured away down here at night, and it does not stop burning when it reaches the dark.

garden_petals.title: A gardener's slate
garden_petals.text: 'The trees were brought from the far east nine hundred years ago, for a girl who missed them. They bloom all year under the glass. Do not ask who the girl was.'

mirror_hall.title: Scratched into gilt
mirror_hall.text: On the frame of the last mirror, very small: a vampire is supposed to have no reflection. In this hall they have hundreds, and none of them is kind.

lab_notes.title: Radu's notes
lab_notes.text: 'Flame grown from Methuselah blood burns hotter than any Terran fire, and it remembers what it was. Batch nine obeyed me for a whole minute. Ion would call this a miracle. Ion would be wrong.'

letter_arcade.title: A letter to Rome (III)
letter_arcade.text: Dear Esther. They say I killed a man in the bazaar. I didn't. Something in my blood carried me through iron bars to prove it, and I am trying not to think about what else it can do. — A.

spice_cache.title: A merchant's ledger
spice_cache.text: Saffron, cardamom, black pepper from the south. And, in a different hand: 'Twelve crates of lamp oil for the gentlemen of the Rose and Cross. Not to be stored near the stalls.'

rooftop_view.title: From the rooftops
rooftop_view.text: Domes of blue tile and gold, all the way to the palace. Somewhere under them the Empress is deciding whether the man from Rome is a guest, a hostage, or a gift.

aqueduct_cache.title: Oil, rags and a rose
aqueduct_cache.text: Cans of lamp oil wrapped in rags, enough to burn a street. On each, a small painted rose on a cross. Someone is going to set the bazaar alight, and it isn't going to look like an accident.

warehouse_manifest.title: A shipping manifest
warehouse_manifest.text: Silk from the east, dyes from the south, and one crate 'for Count Fortuna's household' that was never delivered. The seal on it is not the Fortuna seal.
